text: This school is awesome. Its staff & teachers really care about our education and they are really nice.
It's a great school with great teachers and students!
This is one of the best schools I've ever been to.The teachers are great and the students here make great friends. Academically, this school is at a great level.
Amazing School. Teachers are very nice, helpful and care about the students.
this school is amazing and I love it. everyone is so nice and the teachers are awesome.
This school is the best school I have been to. It is a nice, organized, and friendly school. The teachers are nice and help any individual student that needs help catching up. :)
I am going to this school and love it, it has the best Teachers and great pranciple
It is a great school with the majority of teachers being good and the students are amazing.
It is a great school and the teachers are awesome!

This School is a really great school. I enjoyed my time here and in fact i have grew to be a very responsible person because of this school pushing me in the right direction! The teachers were excellent!

This school is horrible. The teachers are bitter, play favorites, can't do their jobs properly, and do nothing about bullying. The students are mean and bully kids if the child isn't to their standards. The administrators don't care, I know from experience since I was supposed to talk to the principal about something going on involving me getting bullied but he was too "busy" to do it and had me to talk to someone else. Don't send your child here, it's awful and it will put your child through a nightmare. They will literally be terrified to come to school every day.

this school is awful about protecting your child from bullying the administration is awful and needs to be replaced they are very unorganized and sneaky. they school is so overcrowded the kids are squished in the hall changing classes.

I have two children who attend this school. I had to pull one of my students out because they were being bullied. I believe they have a big discipline problem and bullying problem that needs to be addressed.

My school is horrendous. If you're thinking of putting your child in this district you better hope they have the right looks. So much bullying happens here that goes untouched. My family has contacted the principal and he did nothing which leaves the bulling to happen.

I have nothing good to say about this school... if you have an issue you have no way of knowing if it was handled. They care more about protecting their staff than caring for the students. Bullying is at an all new level when the school is whose doing it

Too many students in this school, many of whom do not respect their teachers. Bullying is out of control and the teachers and administration do nothing to stop it. The school is very good at sweeping student issues under the rug. Very disappointed and cannot wait to get my child out of the district at the end of this school year.
This school has great teachers and some of the students there are great. But when I attended there was a lot of bullying going on and the principal would do nothing

This school is administered very poorly, worst school ever. The sad thing is I have gone to the PRINCIPAL for assistance and this Principal who states that BULLYING is not tolerated did not take proper action. Instead it took someone else lower took an initiative to LISTEN and assist. I as well will NEVER put my next child in this poorly administered SCHOOL!

This school is a cesspit. I see kids get bullied all the time and teachers don't deal with the bullies effectively. At most they get a slap on the wrist! NEVER doing any proper justice to the kids who deal with the bullies. This school ENABLES terrible behavior. They only ever punish the kids who are only standing up for themselves cause this school does not help them.

I was a student there from 6th to 10th grade and the school was not decent at all. The students didn't care about the learning or the teachers. They believed that they could do what ever they wanted and they did not act responsible or respectful to anyone. I was bullied there for years and the only way it stopped was when I swung back. The teachers are great and always want to teach and make the best of the year, but the students don't care and stop everything that they have planned. The other problem with the school is that the teachers have no bite. When bullying takes place, they are supposed to have a conference between the two students. You can bring the issue up to the teacher or the principle and no action would be done.
The teachers and staff are great! They go out of there way to help the students and the families. To help make the students successful in all they do
The teachers are great they care about their students. They go above and beyond what is needed when a student needs help.
Excellent, caring teachers and staff. The school’s goal is for each student to reach their potential.
Overall a great experience with teachers and staff who really care about the students.
Great teachers and staff. You can definitely tell they care for the students
Great teachers and staff. The teachers care about the student and go out of their way.
The teachers are great. A lot of activities for the kids to be involved in. A lot of career prep opportunities for the students.
The teachers at this school do a great job and are very dedicated to their students!
The teachers are great and the student leadership is awesome.
Very supportive and engaged teachers. Administration cares about the students. Friendly atmosphere.

If you care about academics, don't send your children to this school The school administrators are inept, the teachers uncaring, and the students small-minded. Really, they just want to move the students through, keep up their sports programs, and keep everyone close to home. Not a good school at all.

This school definitely prepared my child for college but I saw way too many cases of non athletes. Being treated unfairly and treated as second class citizens.I have also seen children of coaches and teachers get away with anything at this school i.e. bullying, smoking jewels, blatant disrespect, etc... but nothing is done b/c daddybis a coach...

I have mixed feelings about this school, the teachers do play favorites and if a student is not in sports, they are treated differently, and not for the better. Serious attention needs to be given to the attitudes of the teachers and staff. Just because a person is not in sports does not mean they will not be a good student. And if a student is struggling, they need help, not ridicule...

I've had several children attend this school so far because of zoning, and every one of them has complained about the lack of attention that teachers, guidance, and administrators give. The sports program is an absolute joke. The coaches claim they have backgrounds in the sport, yet, when I attended reward ceremonies, some of the "coaches" admitted that they did not know a thing about the sport in which they were supposed to coach. The football and baseball coaches are obviously oblivious as to how to teach and train athletes. Unless you ve had some experience in football or baseball elsewhere, don t expect your child to learn anything from these guys. The academics is another fiasco. Students are pigeon-holed into programs and classes without any flexibility. It's virtually impossible to get any satisfaction during any parent-teacher conference because the teachers all come with an attitude that they know better than the parent how the child behaves. This is the worst public school in the area, and I would not be surprised if it was not the worst in the entire country. I will not send any more children to this school.

This school looks good from the outside and that's all there is. It's a travesty. Bullying goes on and on and on. Drugs, fights and nothing but talk from the administrators. Certain kids get away with anything but if one kid is a certain type, nothing will ever come their way. Not to speak of the corrupt sports teams where the same kind of kids make it. Rejection after rejection and again the administrators and so called coaches have excuses. You ask something, they are fake hurt and vehemently defend their nepotistic way. It's a chaotic school that screams Hawk pride while feeding on their young. Worst school by far. Blatant disregard of any kind of fairness while they claim to be so inclusive. An honor student goes to C- yet they advertise their academic programs that fail to address even the most basics in education. An outgoing kid is beaten into submission and anxiety with teachers standing by high fiving the perpetrators. An always athletic kid can't make any of the teams. The disconnect between their always empty words and slogans and propaganda and the reality of projecting fear, disregard, disrespect and exclusion is deafening and scary.

As the parent of a child who attended this school I am very disappointed in the in the overall educational and sports experience she had that this school. I don't feel they prepared her properly for college, they did not challenge her enough in the different subject matters. Their sports programs are among the worse in the city. They allow people with no coaching experience or no knowledge of the sport to be head coaches. They seem to have no idea how important sports can be in the educational process for a student. The current Principal has shown poor leadership and no direction for the school. There are some teachers at this school who do a very good job but there are not enough of them. I will not allow my son to attend this school.

This school is more worried about sports than education. They don’t have a lot of classes to offer. This school is a hick town school, there’s barely any teachers because all they do is fire them for no reason. The students are rude! The teachers have their favorites.

I am sad to say that sports is the only exciting thing about this school. Academic learning by itself is challenging especially for those in Alternative Education, as the Administration of the school low balls students who "don't fit in". Many teachers are disrespectful towards students, which can often be a two way streak, but the amount of targeting and rude remarks done by the teachers is outrageous. In 8th grade, a teacher wrote.me up for being late to class when I was on crutches for a knee surgery. Freshman year I got jumped at school by a junior and was later threatened by the school police officer of fining me with disorder conduct for "antagonizing" the fight. The only thing the staff in this school district prioritize is their paycheck and a grade. I have been raised my whole life in these schools and would never even consider taking kid here when I'm an adult. This school doesn't prepare kids for their life, and if they do, all it shows is the negative things in this world they will encounter.

All this school does is play favorites, put our children at risk and discourage actual learning in any way, shape or form. My child is an A student, good in sports, & his coach treats him like he isn't even there. He hasn't been in trouble either! If I knew then what I knew now, we would have moved to Blue Springs, or Lee's Summit!

My children have excelled in this school and the class offerings are diverse and academically challenging. The electives and extracurricular activities provided are well balanced and lets students bring out their assets. Like most schools in AL, sports programs are treated with the utmost importance, especially football. Admin should try to recognize those that aren't academically inclined more. Luckily the teachers make a fuss when students try their best and do well.

This school offers a ton of AP courses and allows the students to be challenged. My daughter as a Senior chose to take 2 AP courses as electives and was challenged. She is now in college and thriving while others she knows who didn't challenge themselves find college extremely hard. The teachers are great, the coaches are great, the school spirit is wonderful and I have a sophomore there right now.
This school thoroughly prepares your student for college with a wealth of AP and honors classes. Teachers are what make these classes great.

This school far exceeds our expectations. The principal, teachers, and staff have all been quick with correspondence and pleasant. There are so many clubs available making it easy for kids to find their niche and their people. Lots of assistance for kids struggling and rigorous challenging AP classes for the excelling students. It's always clean and a welcoming place.

I love this school. Its kind of huge, but the students mostly get along well. The principals try to know their students and the teacher keep getting better. The AP classes are excellent. Its still high school, so it can be a drag, but i wouldn't want to be anywhere else. At my last school, the teachers didn't even care if you failed.

I am extremely impressed with this school. I was worried after sending my son to private school that he wouldn’t be as successful. He has actually been more challenged by the AP courses that are offered to him.

I am a parent of 2 children who attended and graduated from Ridge. From the administration down to the teachers, everyone was professional and caring. The quality of the teaching staff, their dedication and willingness to spend outside time helping and tutoring students is amazing. The school has one of the top rated AP curriculum's in the state, incredible passing stats, a great honors program. One student of mine took majority honors and AP classes, my other student took Honors, Dual Enrollment and AP classes. They have prepared my kids for college and the challenges they will face.
This school is so great . It offers many great AP classes and the teachers are so dedicated to their jobs.

A top notch school that has high test scores and sends nearly all students on to higher education. Academics are a top priority and several AP classes have been added in past years. They offer a wide variety of athletics and extra-curriculars where students also perform well. The school is not huge, your child will not get lost. Parents are actively involved and they expect top results. The staff is young, enthusiastic, and they make good use of new technology in the classroom.

My son went there for grades 6-12. We could not have been more pleased. He had opportunities to meet people from different towns and has a strong sense of self. The teachers were great and deeply invested in his success. He had a chance to play varsity sports and lots of clubs and activities. The school deliberately does not offer AP classes, but instead offers classes at the honors level for everyone. This school is designed for great college acceptances, and the formula worked. His class had two kids go to Yale and one to Princeton. Most of his classmates found success in college and are now prepared for life after college. You don’t need to be miserable cramming for AP exams to be ready for college. Learn to Read, Write, Think, Problem Solve and Communicate. The liberal arts foundation combined with knowledge of the classics gives the students the chance to live up to the motto non scholae see vitae discimus rings true. While my son graduated in 2016, I hear the principal - a former Classical teacher is doing a great job to reinstill the Gladiator pride. His friends are great kids who are interesting and driven and they represent the diversity that makes our society stronger. If you want to pick a school based on AP scores, you will miss this gem of school, and miss the point of being at a magnet school in the first place.

This school has given me many opportunities to take challenging courses both AP level and honors. I feel that the teachers have prepared me for college throughout all four years and each teacher wanted to see every student succeed.

I graduated from this school and I loved in. All the teachers and all the administration were amazing with me including going through my senior year while my father was ill and dying of lung cancer. They were all very understanding and helpful emotionally and with my academics. The students were also amazing, I had lots of friends, being far from 'Popular'. There was very little teasing or bullying at all which was a huge change from the other school I had been at.
My experience at this school was wonderful
I graduated here and enjoyed my experience as a student a lot. Teachers were always helpful, I felt I had a great education from this school.
This school was amazing. They had great resources and teachers to help students like myself to be successful in both college and life.
As a former student, I can attest to the superb atmosphere, teachers, and staff at High School North. I loved the school and the opportunities it provided me.
i liked attending this school very much the teachers were excellent and i loved the experience!

I attended this school from 2008-2009 and graduated. I loved it! The teachers were fun, the students were sociable, and the variety of classes that are offered to you are more than sufficient when applying to colleges.
My experience at this school was amazing.

I graduated 2 years ago, and I found the teachers and learning environment very inspiring. I loved the small community, extracurricular activities, and everything the school had to offer! It's quaint and comfy. The academics were good, too.
My experience at this school was amazing!

This is a great school for well-rounded students! Aside from having talented and supportive teachers and staff it offers way more curriculum variety and after school activities that aren't available at other schools.The Art and music departments have won many awards are the best in the area!

This is a great school with involved staff! It has a ver approachable atmosphere and lots of opportuninty for student growth, It's challenging for my kids, in a good way. IThey are getting a good education and I feel like the teachers really care.They have a great music department and take pride in their sports teams! A+

This is a phenomenal school with fantastic teachers. It has great community involvement and much to offer students. Anyone saying they don't value arts, clearly hasn't been to a band competition, school play, or a recital. The arts are strong and continue to improve. The school is also strong with athletics and extra-curricular activities. A student can easily get involved in this school.
Band/overall Arts Program are the only good things about this school. Seriously.

My children have done well at this school. We've NEVER had a problem with this school in any way. The teachers have been great. Their music program is superb, and we've really enjoyed it. The bands and choirs win competitions everywhere they go. I far prefer this school to the one my children had to go to in California. Thumbs up.

We have two students now going to this school and they love it. Has a great Marching Band and director, plus, can't say enough about our principal who has turned this school around in a short period of time and make us proud of it. Thanks to all their hard work. PS. Love the art programs there.

This is a wonderful school as long as the students and parents put in their fair share, the teachers and staff are not there to do all of the work. The music program is wonderful and the music teachers go above and beyond for their students.

As a parent of current students, I find the school to be great! The teachers are engaged and dedicated to the education of the students. The current superintendent and board of directors are dedicated to constantly evaluating and working toward the improvement of the academic curriculum. Extracurricular activities are diverse and, because the school is of moderate size, the opportunities for a student to participate in these activities is outstanding. There are never 80 kids vying for 18 spots on the team! There is truly something for every student who wants to be involved. The music program starts in elementary school and engages and inspires students early. Several bands, orchestras and choral opportunities to choose from, an outstanding program! Multiple art classes offered. Recent improvements to the building including air conditioning, new science and music/arts wing. Updated, spacious facilities. Most importantly this is a great community where people know each other. Family involvement is welcomed in the school community. Parents can get to know their kids teachers, coaches and mentors and communication is encouraged. Many parents are alumni!
This school is amazing, great programs and the teachers are excellent. The Chorus is an amazing class, the bond between the students there is unbelievable. Couldn't get any better!

I went on a tour of the school and I was very impressed on what they had to offer. I liked everything about the school. I think I will be sending my child there next year. If you like arts and music this is the school to go to :)

My son was at top of the line public school but, he was highly ignored by the teachers and overly dependent on an aide. Many things were done wrong including placing him on a 1st grade classroom just because it was a full day program. I fought the school district and got him placed at Village Glen. He is now in the 3rd grade, has friends, the teachers and the principal are super nice and he is actually learning. They are receptive to my concerns and are able to accomodate even if it is not on the IEP. My daughter also attended one of their schools too with severe psychiatric problems and was able to finish HS and go to college. They do an excellent job with a very challenging population. All school districts should emulate their model of teaching students with special needs.

This school is amazing! My child has special needs (he has an IEP), so we have to request special help from his teachers on a daily basis. These teachers go above and beyond our expectations. They always keep you in the loop and most of them will send home several progress reports so that you can see how your child is doing before the official report card comes out. This helps you in making sure that your child is caught up and has turned in all assignments, etc. There was a new principal last school year who put a few new practices into place. Though I'm not pleased with them, we have adapted with no problems. There is one person in the office who can be less than pleasant, but that's really the only negative I can think of.

Two years here and numerous incidents jeopardizing my child's health. If you have a child with special needs of any sort, this is not the school for your family. They are too busy, disorganized, and unprofessional to handle anything other than the "typical" student and there is a very apparent disconnect between administration and teachers, and then both display bare minimum communication with students and parents. Every area of this school needs proper training and some sort of team building so they actually work together.

I am not satisfy with this school. The Staff don't do their jobs correctly. Especially for kids with special needs, this is not the appropriate school. The teachers don't do their job right and are not even train for students with special needs. There is no good program for it. They can't even control the situation when a a student disability throws a tantrum. The staff train for it takes the student outside, which is more dangerous, in other to calm them down. They don't have the proper staff when it comes to IEP meeting. They don't even complete the goals. They let the student's with disability do what they want, they don't even notice if they're in class or not. Not even good for counseling the students with disabilities. This is not the proper school for Special Ed students. They don't have a program for them at all.
My son with special needs was bullied at this school. The administration did not provide adequate support. I made many requests for help which were unanswered. I would not recommend this school.

I have a child with special needs, and the school's response has been fabulous. They go out of their way to follow her IEP, and ensure all of her teachers are aware and working with her the way they are supposed to. We are having a great experience halfway through her first year there. Our son graduated last year and did very well. Good preparation for college. It's a great school.

I have had four kids in this school, one with special needs. He has ADHD and Aspberger's Disorder. The special education department has not been helpful at all with regards to my child. Also, 2 of my children have been able to ditch and they have taken and bought marijuana at school. This is not a drug free zone nor an A+ school. This school does not do what our kids need, especially now that the economy is what it is. That is why they no longer have a resource officer to police our kids, so now they can get away with more stuff.
If your child needs special ed services, be ready to fight for them. For the average child, it's a great school system.

Terrible school if your child has special needs and requires a 504 plan or IEP. Overall the school either does not know how to help special needs kids or they just do not want to. There are some great individual teachers and then there are some terrible ones. And the administration seems like their mission in life is to make sure they help kids the minimum amount possible. I have been told many times that they are "too busy" to properly help my child, that they have too many students. Most seem to have learned their special needs knowledge from a text book and refuse to apply it individually to your childs needs. Or thyley blame my child and act like he/she is lazy since they are unable to successfully address my child's issues. I'm sure this school seems find if you only have typical kids.

As a parent I was not impressed with this school. Teacher quality is not very high, the current principle did not return any phone calls or emails concerning an important issue. The politics and desire to fill quotas for their "Special Education" is more of a priority to the school than delivering the extra help needed.

This is an academically challenging school that has so much spirit. The administration is committed to this school, its mission and each student. My daughter is a sophomore and loves her school. I have had other children attend other high schools and have not been nearly as impressed. The IB program is amazing. Teacher connect with students, something for every girl at this school.

This school and its ib program are great. My son has been going here for 2 years, and he's been doing amazing in each and every one of his classes. This school wouldn't be as great as it is without its ib program. Overall, great school!
I have my son and my daughter in this school they are very happy they say that the school is much more better that they expected. academically they are doing very well in the IB program.

The school is great. It is well run, the students are in uniform and the halls are quiet and orderly. The IB program is wonderful. It is very vigorous and really prepares students for college. The teachers are top rate. There are also many AP courses available. Generally we have been very satisfied with the caliber of learning that is expected and the range of classes offered.

This school has been great so far! The IB program my daughter is involved in is wonderful. The school is more intimate and has a family feel. There are still plenty of opportunities for variety but it does not seem to be overwhelming to my student.
This is a fantastic well-rounded school with many academic options. The IB program is top notch.

Honestly, I am an IB student and the school is amazing. It exceeds with offerings that even regular students can take advantage of there is an abundance of programs other than IB like dual credit, AP, pre-ap, pre-ib, and cte classes. The schools have some wonderful teachers and it's really the students that won't pay attention. The school offers many opportunities for students to look at colleges and receive information on a lot of colleges. If parents were more active in their child's education the school could get so much more done.

Small High School- great principal and the IB program is outstanding. Years ago it had a mixed reputation - but today it is considered fantastic. Don't believe what people "used to say" about the school... it's a whole story today!
The IB program is great and the school is surprisingly classy.......The teachers and administration team are absolutely amazing!

Our son has had a good experience there. He has challenging classes and the school has excellent AP and honors level teachers for demanding subjects. We will have two children at the school next year and are looking at the IB program for our second one.
This school has been a blessing for my daughter. The teachers and staff are wonderful and caring. She is college bound and I have experienced a special focus for the students succeed.

My children loved this school so much. They both graduated and are now going to good colleges. Teachers are good and effective, students are nice and welcoming. The school challenged their academic abilities and helped them greatly.
My child has had a great experience at this school. The teachers are committed and supportive. Students are encouraged to achieve in all areas of interest.

I have never seen my son so happy for succeding so great in this school. This school really has made a huge positive impact in his life. He is finishing his 1st year with the "Highest Honor" in the school. We are really happy for his success.

Very happy with my child's education at this school. The classes have been engaging and challenging, my child is learning real-world experiences as well as getting to try classes she is interested in as a career. The school is a tight-knit community, the kids are supportive of one another across all groups (no cliques), and they have great school spirit. I feel my daughter is having the ultimate high school experience.

We have been very happy with this school. The classes have been challenging as our daughter was used to making As without much effort in public school. The teachers here are caring and our daughter has made good friends. The school offers lots of opportunities to be involved for everyone.
Our experience in this school has been beyond excellent. My son and daughter are successful adults, in no small part, because of the efforts of Central High School.
This school has been very good for my son who is in his third year there. We are so impressed with the school that we now have enrolled our second son with them as well.

My son was fully prepared for college and has graduated. My daughter is about to follow in his footsteps. The school is great, they educate and teach them about compassion and try to create non selfish children! I am very happy with this school!
My child received a fantastic education at this school. The teachers really care. The curriculum is dynamic and challenging.

This is the first year my daughter attended this school. They have a high turnover in teachers. However, they provide tutoring for students with school work. The school has no control over racism and would be very uncomfortable for any minority.

I graduated in 2013, This school is not a school to send your children. This school administrations shows racial favoritism. They have no control over the student body. The teachers allow bulling and verbal attacks from the student to both them and the other students.

This school is horrible, horrible, horrible. There is not very much diversity. A third of the school are caucasians, and the rest are african americans. The discipline from the teachers is herendous! The classrooms get out of control according to my daugher, and some of the teachers don't know how to handle the students! People get out their I-Pods, and cameras in class and do whatever they feel like. If I were you, I would not send your child to this school.

This school can be great at times; however, it is most certainly not a good place for minority students. The discrimination that happens at this school is astonishing. And nothing gets done about it. Only given students slaps on the wrist for blatantly threatening the safety of others and saying racial slurs.

The school is plagued with racism, lies and unjust treatment. The lack of diversity speaks for itself. The community is beautiful but our children have called racial terms on many occasions however that does not reference the majority of residents, we have have some great neighbors but some have spoiled the experience.

Hidden and blatant racism is more than evident at this school. I was saddened when my daughter came home and said children choose to segregate themselves at lunch (and the principles not addressing this) and racist remarks as well as disparaging treatment from teachers often occur. The fact that this school is 15min from the heart of our diverse city of Atlanta is simply appalling.

EXTREMELY RACIST school and I am very unhappy to say that I graduated from here. There are several racist and sexist issues to date that have still not been handled and involves several alums dating back to as far as 2016. More specific reasons not to send your kid(s) to this school are the price (why are you willing to pay thousands of dollars for your kids to be discouraged and experience real world issues at the early age of 2), disrespectful faculty and admin (there are lots of bad apples in the bunch of Ursuline Academy staff), many of the incidents that are reports go unanswered are will most definitely be swept under the rug, and to top it off this school will not display equality, diversity, and inclusion, and will do the exact opposite to protect the people who built their system and the government system which are whites.

This school does not support children of color emotionally, socially, or academically. Children are faced with issues of racism, which is just being swept under the rug. The people put in place for student support is not as helpful when it comes to children of color. There is not enough diversity amongst teachers and other faculty. Black children and other children of color are bullied everyday and the school wants to vote on diversity during strategic planning instead of diversity support being an automatic process in place to support students that are attending the school. This is a very microaggressive environment. Teachers and students have been guilty of microaggression towards students of color. This accepted behavior is mentally, emotionally, and academically scarring for kids. It instills a lack of confidence and in some ways abusive to have to endure verbal abuse and microaggression just to be gaslighted and disregarded. This school needs diversity training, and a more diverse faculty to promote cultural sensitivity.

We are so happy to be at a school that is welcoming to children of color and differences. Our daughter is much happier than previous schools where she experienced racism and exclusion. This school makes a big effort to include all and to lift each child up to a place of confidence and individual capability.

Its not a really diverse school , if you're looking for a school with diversity this is not the school. The staff is okay but it could be better. A lot of the kids are racist and are not really held accountable for things that they do . Many kids do drugs or sell drugs here and get away with it and hide it really well from the teachers .

Teachers are good, but the administration needs extreme improvement. Tries to pretend to be a private school. Has suspended a student over a Tweet and a student has been reprimanded for petitioning. Principal does not make herself available to students.

Great Kids and Teachers. Administration (basically the principal and one of the assistant principals) is ruining the school. Teacher are leaving in droves because of their treatment and the school board (even though addressed about it many times) fails to fix the situation.

There are a few GREAT leaders at this school, the guidance counselor and the elementary principal particularly. However, the school board and the superintendent are ignorant and hateful, unqualified for their jobs. I'm not sure anyone on the school board has even been to college. The superintendent is disconnected from the school and could care less about the students. Most of the teachers aren't qualified and have no business being in charge of children. The kids are great, but deserve much better from the teachers and administrators at this school.
The administration is worthless, mostly the principal. It is basically the boys club and their only purpose is to intimidate and bully the teachers.
Poor leadership. Not worth the money. Principal is useless. Found another school that better suited our needs.
This is a case of great school gone very bad. New principal is beyond awful. Does not know the 1st thing about leadership.

The administration cares more about appearances and paperwork than actually teaching the students. The administration does not honor the teacher contract and treats the staff like errant children. My daughter just graduated in 2016 from Saint Joseph High School, and we feel that this was the best decision we could've made. She was able to reach her full potential thankfully to all the advanced classes that the this school offers. She also had the opportunity to enjoy different clubs and partake in many service opportunities provided through the school. I really recommend it for parents that are looking for a great school for their daughters, you are NOT going to regret it ever.

St. Anthony's is a wonderful school. Their academics and sports are great. The best part is the discipline. Although I felt it was too harsh as a student there, I know now it was the best for us. It kept us in line and concentrating on what was important. Only now I appreciate it even more being that I work in a public school in Brooklyn! The tuition is high but well worth it.

My daughter has thrived at St. Francis. The academics are challenging, and her teachers are accessible and encouraging if she has any questions or problems with a course. Her confidence has risen. There are numerous extra curricular activities for students to become involved with, and she is taking the opportunity to explore different clubs and interests. She is getting a good foundation academically and spiritually for life after high school.

St. Michael has been an excellent choice for my daughter. The test scores are very good and the academic program is challenging. She has felt at home since her freshman year. I, as a parent, appreciate the strict discipline policies and requirements. I feel the students are taught respect for themselves and others. Parents are very involved and there is a great amount of school pride. The school hasn't been around as long as some of the other high schools in town, but with time I think it will prove to be just as good.

St. Mary's Reich in high school was an excellent education. It is college prep and compared to my friends in public school the workload was much larger. The discipline and writing abilities that I developed at Ryken's program helped me to excel in college and with getting my CPA and MBA. I have kept in touch with all of my classmates through Facebook over the years and nearly all of them have graduated from colleges all over the country some returning to the area and some not. The relationships formed with students and faculty in this small school are valuable and long-lasting friendships. I also believe that many of the teachers feel that they have a higher purpose in educating the students because of their Christian values and dedication to service which is why they go above and beyond helping their students anyway possible. I would highly recommend this high school and hope to be able to send my children there one day.
This is a fantastic school, giving all the girls an equal chance to excel in all subjects. The teachers are phenomenal and St Mary's is a great school and one of the best experiences in my life.

South has been a great experience. It's smaller than other schools and the teachers and administrators know and care about the kids. Students also get great opportunities to participate in school life via sports and clubs. And our daughter has also gotten to know students from around the world, which has been an invaluable and unique experience. The academics have been challenging, and AP classes interesting, relevant and engaging. I strong recommend South to students and parents who are looking for a place where they're supported, engaged, and can have an interesting experience in a culturally diverse environment. Read the Newcomers by Helen Thorpe to get some of the flavor of the school

South was pretty great for my son. The teachers were very caring and committed. The dean of students was amazing. The principal Scott McDowell was horrendous. He cares about the sports program and the honors program. He did not address parent concerns and was actually not even sympathetic.

I am a freshman at South and I absolutely adore it. The teachers are phenomenal, the student body is very diverse(something you won't find at many other high schools in the metro) and the community is very welcoming. I play sports, which I have found to be very helpful as a way of meeting other kids, particularly upperclassmen. I also play in band and I am sure that South has the best band program in the state. Our director is amazing, by far the best teacher I have ever had.The kids are talented, hardworking and just love music. I would highly recommend this school!

I am fully in support of my children attending our neighborhood school and not cherry picking the system. We are feel so fortunate that South is our neighborhood school. The diversity, and the lack of cliques at this school is rare indeed. The culture is one of encouragement and cooperation. And the rigor of the classes cannot be denied - South High grads will be well prepared to attend any college or pursue any other endeavor that they wish. As a parent I was a little stunned at the level of demand from the students academically - but am seeing the results and realizing just how much high school students are capable of achieving. I would give it all 5 stars but I see the school getting even better under Dr. Waters leadership.. so leaving room for that process! I highly recommend South as a parent.. (oh and my student loves it as well!)
South is a great school. the 4 years I went there were the best. All most all the teachers were nice. only 2 that i had problems with. The choir there was great too.
South is overall a good school, but some small tweaks to bring back, what I feel, made it great.

We had four children go through the John Jones Elem., Southside Elem. and Southside HS schools and we couldn't be happier w/the results. All four have completed college (w/honors) and I give a very large amount of credit to the Southside areas schools. No school is perfect and there's always room for improvement in any school but, academics, sports and all extracurricular activities are as good at Southside as you'll find anywhere.

Although this school is much older compared to all the other schools in the district, South Lake High is an excellent school with great teachers and staff as well as spirit. For all four years of my high school career, I do not regret going to this school, it's like home and I'm so sad to be graduating soon. The school offers a variety of courses as well as extra curricular activities. The staff shows pride in their students and they always praise us. The teachers not only educate students on course material, they also expand the subject and they help inform students about how the course material affects our world.

I joined South at the start of my junior year. Everyone was so welcoming, especially the students. I was amazed at the top class quality of teaching. However, what stood out to me the most was the amount of extracurricular activities this school has to offer. You’ll find a club for ANY special interests at high school South.

The principal at this school is fantastic and very responsive. My daughter is enjoying her teachers and is in the honors program here as well as track. I have not regretted sending my daughter here at all! I think that Southridge is an all-around great school and they truly care about the kids. I do wish the drama and music programs were even better, and that the parents were more involved, but I believe that lack of parental involvement is becoming an epidemic all over the U.S.

This school is full of teachers and staff who genuinely care about your kids. Alot of the bad issues other schools have are very low in number here or non existent. The school counselors are great with helping students decide on classes that mirror their future plans.
Although the counselors in this school seemed to try their best; the school is simply too large to be a great school. Kids are herded through classes with little to no individual help from teachers.

My biggest problem is the school does not care about the kids. They have a teacher that gets multiple complaints but they do nothing and they have no option because she is the only one that teaches that class and it is a required class for all students to graduate. The principle and dean support her and not the students. Many of the teachers are great, but not all of them. I am very thankful for the understanding and support of the counselors. They are amazing.

Unfortunately the quality of teachers for most subjects is very poor. The counselors are just not helpful and I see that public school counselors are doing much better handling many more kids. Though the school claims to prepare students for college, i do not see any indication so far! I'm very disappointed and strongly encourage parents to stay away from this school. It is a complete waste of money.

Overall, its an esthetically pleasing atmosphere. The classrooms are clean, the grounds are very nice, and the number of students enrolled is nice. We like a small town feel. However, the Staff is extremely disengaged. They don't interact with parents unless the parents reach out to them. They also don't utilize their counselor. There are several kids I know of who clearly would benefit from counseling and as a Counselor, I personally would be on the lookout for red flags or warning signs. It seems that the counselors only job is on an "As Needed" basis. The principal is pleasant to deal with but she should also be working with the counselor for students struggling academically to ensure they get the best shot.

While this school is great in some aspects, the teachers are either hit or miss. I have had some truly amazing teachers who really did their job well. On the other hand, there are some teachers that were clearly there to get their ten year and muddle through the next 30 years. Additionally, due to the amount of students, if you don't stand out in your counselor's mind they do basically nothing for you and make it very difficult to get any classes changed around without a parent present to pressure them into doing what they should be able to handle with the students. Great opportunities for those who want to take advanced classes, but depending on the teacher the student will need to be able to take control of teaching themselves a class.

The teachers and coaches at this school are good and work hard with their limited resources. The administration is the problem here. They are unresponsive and make a lot of bad assumptions. The counselors have not been helpful with providing information and support for my college bound students. This school could do a much better job of partnering with parents and being proactive. When I called to speak with the principle about a problem I saw, I was told I could come speak if I liked but he WOULD NOT change his position. Not very much of a partnership.

the teachers are great, my son loves the school. I wish the Guidance counselors would become more involved in the kids lives call them in talk about College, there plans in life, incourage them. when I was in high school our counselors called us in each 9 weeks to just talk, about the future, and if we were on track...

My experience at this school was very negative. Most of the teachers did not care about the experience that they were giving their students. Obviously there were the exceptions. The counselors are also very self centered. They don’t care about students wishes but rather the easy way out.

The school administration and counselors are horrible. They want what is best or convenient to them not the students. Many students get punished over stupid reasons or for stuff they don't do. I have only had 2 or 3 teachers who have actually cared about their students instead of teach for tests and looks. Many teachers don't care about their students. The sports team is a big joke. Jackupson worst coach ever. The only thing good about the school is the technology and the band. Other than that I recommend another school.

There are some fantastic teachers here that inspire students to learn and grow. Fortunately, we've experienced some of them. Unfortunately, they are the exception. This school is plagued with petty, power tripping tyrants that harass students over minor issues, give less than achieved grades when parents dare to question what or why they are teaching a certain way, fail to communicate with parents, and the politics and favoritism within the athletics department is awful, etc. Kids with amazing potential get lost in the maze, harassed by administration, and lose all confidence and momentum to succeed. My child is a Freshman at CHS, I can count more times she has come home crying than I can good days and no one at the school cares, and I am told more often than not that it is "her fault". I moved into the district so that she could go to this school based on the things I was told and am moving out of the district and to a different school based on the ACTUAL experience.

We moved here 5 years ago and I thought the schools were good at the time. I had one child in 6th grade and one child in 3rd grade at the time. However, the schools have really gone downhill over the last 2-3 years. My daughter transferred out to a charter school 2 years ago in the middle of the 9th grade because the high school was just not challenging enough for her. They do not have anything to offer advanced students and she was very bored academically. My son transferred to an online school last year due to slipping grades, bullying, and absolutely no help from the staff at the middle school. The online grade book is not updated regularly. My son once spent two days straight in lunch detention because a teacher put demerits under his name by mistake. When my son tried to ask why he was in there, he was told to sit down and be quiet. When I called the principal to complain, he acted as though it was just a mistake and no big deal. My son was also beaten up at the bus stop once and the school said they could do nothing about it because he was not on the bus or school grounds.

The administration at this school is terrible. Completely irrational and unreasonable. When there are issues, they don't want to hear about it. They automatically blame students for issues without doing their due diligence and getting to the root cause of problems. More than once, issues came up that the teachers and administration assigned as issues with my child, only to later discover that the teachers were the problem, proved by data. Status on school work is a chronic problem - teachers not giving students credit for assignments, errors in grading, etc. Keep ALL of your student's work and be prepared to verify EVERYTHING related to grading. The communication is really bad -- don't expect answers to email or returned phone calls. They just don't want to hear from parents. They site a 48-response time to email and other inquiries in the student handbook, that they don't adhere to in the least. When you insist on speaking with them, you can muster up a meeting but, ultimately, they are just humoring you...It's 'their way or the highway'. I'm SO sorry that I placed my child in this school, and am looking into other options.

This school is abysmal when it comes to communication. My child struggled immensely during his four years here and I found that his teachers didn’t return emails or phone calls when I reached out for help. When I turned to the principal for help, I was advised to just continue emailing and calling and if I did get a response, it was usually when grades were already submitted or it was too late to redeem his grade. Finally, during his senior year, I contacted my son's guidance counselor to arrange a meeting with his teachers and took time off from my new job, which I didn’t mind doing since I value my child’s education. I even confirmed a time that work best for the teachers, since I know they are not required to stay after 4pm. Unfortunately the teachers did not place the same value on my child’s education, and when I arrived, I was told that none of the teachers showed up. They all had a variety of excuses even though they had all confirmed they would attend, and the principal and superintendent were dismissive when I escalated my complaint (“I’m sorry that happened to you but things come up”). The only time I received any communication was when my son's substitute lost the remote control and decided to illegally search all of the students. My son questioned the teacher’s right to do this and the Vice Principal called me to say my son was "mouthing off". The remote was later found in the substitute’s possession. Trust me, send your child to another school if you value their education.

I am absolutely appalled at this school. My family and I moved here a year and a half ago from up north. My child had wonderful grades. It took over 4 weeks for the school to review her records and place her in appropriate classes. So, she gets her schedule and not one administrative person offers to show her where her classes are. Never mind the fact that most of the classes she had already taken previously. The teachers were rude and had no problems swearing and putting on movies instead of teaching. Now we are in her second year at this school. Teachers have blatantly refused to help her out with any of the work she doesn't understand. She has complained that many of them say to the students if you don't want to listen then I won't teach you. When she speaks up about this, she gets sent to the office! I have had many conversations with the "drop out prevention specialist" who has demeaned my child numerous times and threatened to have her sent to an alternative school. Then when I demanded a meeting with her and administration I was met with just on of her teachers instead. This school is an absolute joke. The are disorganized and refuse to make any changes with their staff. Oh, and forget parent teacher night. This is a joke as well. I have gone to every single one offered over the last year and a half. I have met only 3 of her teachers in two years. The others were not even there! I am now considering home schooling my daughter for her last year. These should be the best years of my daughters life!

This school is horrible and is ran by a man that has no tolerance for kids. He rather suspend kids and remove them from class than help them, counsel them, and teach them if they make a small mistake. Suspension is the ONLY form of dicipline. There are no warnings. My son has always been the quiet kid who never got in trouble until now. If you want your child to grow in their confidence and be all they can possibly be I would not send them to this school where they make up their own rules, consequences and do not follow any standards. Not to mention my kids have hardly had any homework and I have never seen so much teacher turnover in one year! My child's "honor" classes Have not been challenging and both of their study habits have declined due to lack of homework. They make the school look good with all the activities but there are silly rules with that as well. They had the Phoenix police that work for the principal search my daughters belongings with parental knowledge looking for someone else's Iphone, which they eventually found somewhere else.. no apology or comment to us as parents regarding the incident either. They also limit the activities and put restrictions on doing art and sports. You cannot do both st the same time. Where as most schools encourage as much student involvement and work together as coaches/teachers. Lastly, they do not encourage parental involvement within the school. The principal wants it all done his way there is no reasoning, or talking to him. Also he is Very insensitive and has terrible people skills. I would strongly advise anyone looking into this school to look elsewhere.

Chaparral High School is one of the worst schools my daughter has ever been to. Not only based on her experiences and opinions but mine as a parent as well. They literally kick the students off school grounds during split class when lunch time is not available, at the end of the school year they demand to have the students belongings and hold them for two full days before returning them. That doesn't even make sense! As a parent I don't understand many of there practices. The teachers are horrible at mediating conflicts, as if they don't care about there students. My daughter was bothered many times throughout the year by other male students within her class while the teachers said nothing ,even when she reported this to the teacher, I can go on but I am running out of word count. I am currently filing many complaints concerning there school system. Please do not enroll your kids in this school. You may regret it as I have. (

I also have to agree with everything the previous poster said. It is very difficult to get ahold of anyone in the summer months, as the counselors work minimal hours. we just moved to the area from out of state. I have emailed at least 10 people in that school through the year with no response. The classes are overcrowded. one class my child is in has 38 kids. They are expecting over 400 new students for the 2017/2018 school year and they are already over crowded and has portables on order. Many of the teachers are terrible. They hold morning hours for the students that need help,(if they show up for them) but when my child went she was told, that she should know the material already and the teacher didn't help. then I tried to email other teachers in that department with no response. One day after school started my child was having problems and went to the office to talk to a counselor, she was told to fill out a slip and the counselor would call her in. Days later no call until I complained to someone in the office. Also if you come from a small town, do not expect this school to be like that, its huge, and unless your child is in the top 1% at a sport, they will not make the team, unless they have been there for years and already a favorite. if you do make the team, expect to shell out Thousands of dollars to play on them. oh and they want money for everything since most families in the school are very wealthy, they don't think of the hardships they put on the rest of the families. When we moved here I didn't have a way to check schools besides this website. I wish more would have spoke up so I could have known what its really like. PS if you are planning to move to the area, keep in mind that over 20000 more homes have been approved to be built. so more overcrowding, not just with the schools, but the roads too. They need traffic controllers at the entrance to the school because there is only one entrance to the school and it literally takes 15 minutes to just pull into the parking lot...St. Johns County needs to get this under control and build another High School.

Teachers are inconsistent with keeping posted grades up to date, are disorganized with and sometimes cryptic with posting assignments and instructions. Often they take awhile to respond to parents requests. Guidance at school is mediocre Mrs. Bobay, the school guidance Counselor and others do work hard to do what's best for students, but I've had trouble with getting the staff to see things through to improve my child's performance or see their plans through to completion. I constantly struggled with my child son who always complained about not liking the school. I ve applied for a n out of area transfer as advised by other parents in my neighborhood. CHS has the potential to be a great school being directly behind a college. Sr. Staff is quick to suspend students for relatively minor infractions, where detentions would have been warranted in any other school. Once a student is suspended (In School) they are supposed to be afforded the opportunity to complete all class work for that day in ISS, but teachers do not submit class work for student to work on, and often will count the student absent instead. Every class drops almost a full letter grade for this type of disconnect.

My child wanted to go into education field for a career. She now wants nothing to do with education. She sees great teachers abused and treated rudely by the principle. This is sad, because she really enjoys some of her classes. A new teacher/coach this year used their power over my my child to show whom is in charge, she dismisses & taunts my daughter numerous times, when I asked the VP/AD to check; he responded with, "Everything looks fair to me." I then questions, "You know who my child is?" He responded, "No." My child is on Honor Roll, a great kid. However this year she genuinely hasn't wanted to go to school and has become depressed. Beaware of the administration at this school, they treat the kids with intimidation and power. The PUSD response, "They are new to their job." Something needs to change. Kids only get once for their high school years.
I currently attend clark high school and i am glad to say that it is a very good school. This school is very pro student, its all about the students, they have great teachers.

This school is awesome! My son had a great experience there. We were so happy we brought a house in Belleville East district. Especially after seeing the disturbing violence at Belleville West making national news.
The students and teachers are great! I wouldn't want to go to any other school. I love clark

This is my daughters junior year at Clarksville High and it has been a good experience. There are lots of clubs, sports, band and choir to participate in and I love the way the school encourages school spirit. Overall a great school.

Springville High School has been an excellent experience for my kids. They have loved their teachers and the curriculum. Two daughters have enjoyed the quality band program and one son has played on the baseball and baskerball teams. They have all worked hard and excelled in their education. My youngest will graduate this spring with a 4.0 gpa and go on to college, as her siblings have done. We couldn't have asked for a better high school experience.

I find one of the best aspects of Rockville HS is its small size. The faculty know all the students and the students all know each other. Most of the teachers have been good or great and all of the faculty and staff are really interested in the kids. The whole school is a close knit community. There are a number of great academic programs including the IB program, engineering program, and journalism program along with a computer science curriculum. There are a lot of extracurricular activities so most students are involved in at least one activity and many are involved in multiple clubs or sports, which adds to the overall involved community feel. I am really glad for my children to be a part of such a great school.
We have enjoyed the Beckville Jr. High School. The principal is really on top of things. The school has great technology and facilities. The classes are small and students are pretty well behaved.

Pleasantville has an outstanding education program from kindergarten to grade 12. The students mostlly all go to college and are well prepared for life. I am also very impressed with the community and the wonderful parents that get involved. It is so nice that all three schools are in walking distance and that the library is accessible after school.

My daughter came here after a below-par experience at a local private school. She has had an excellent 3 years here so far. Rockville High School has a special program to cater for gifted children, she has been achieving better grades and the teachers are for the most part fantastic.

Starkville High School has excellent academic, athletic and extracurricular programs. Both of my children graduated from there recently and were well prepared for college. Lots of university professors send their kids there. The academic offerings are better than any other options in the area. Many teachers there have won statewide awards. Starkville is a great place to raise a family. One reason is its strong public schools.
I love this school district. Teachers & staff are great and my son loves it too
I loved this school district. I graduated from it, my kids also graduated from it and now my grandson is attending school here. This school district wants nothing but the best for their students.
This school district has been great for my children.

I love this school district. A small home town family feel...great communication with the teachers. Each student is known for the person they are, instead of just being a number. Administration is very great at communicating with the parents
Wonderful school district! Teachers truly care about the students individual needs, and are willing to go above and beyond for their students. Very proud to be a member of this community!

I love this school district. They take time to help our kids, they care and they make sure they are always safe. The kids learn to respect each other mo matter what differences they may have from financial to special needs. They grow up ready to face the next chapter in their lives. Thanks to all the students teachers and administrators for making this a great educational experience.

This is a great school district! The staff are caring, compassionate and dedicated. Every student will leave this district with a quality education and the tools they need to become awesome citizens of our society.
Great district! There are a plethora of opportunities for the students, impressive school spirit, awesome high school guidance staff, and many resources available!
Awesome district. Really care about the kids and give great interventions for all types of learners!
Excellent school district.They care about everything and maintenance on the schools are good.

BHS is a great school for middle of the road kids who fit inside a certain box. For everyone else - advanced kids, kids with any kind of learning disability, kids who are not totally into sports - I would not recommend this school at all. One of my kids ended up doing running start to get away, the other begged to go to a different school. Rampant drug and alcohol abuse, serious eating disorders in girls, slut shaming posing as "health education" (using the duct tape talk) all contribute to an atmosphere that is not a positive place for learning.

I really enjoyed going attending BHS, and learned many valuable skills that I still use to this day. It is a relatively small school so there is plenty of one of one teacher/student time available if wanted. The school does a great job of making higher level classes available for those that are eager to learn.

BHS is great! I graduated from the Belchertown Junior Senior High School and I am proud to say that my son will be graduating from BHS next year. He is learning and enjoying himself by participating in a variety of activities.

My oldest son just graduated from BHS. We have had a wonderful experience at this school. He graduated with honors and has had some truly exceptional teachers in his four years there. There are so many extra curricular activities at this school, that every student should be able to find something that interests them, and the teachers and staff devote a lot of their time before and after school to make sure that these programs continue to grow every year. Thank you teachers, staff, and administration!!!

BHS is the a nationally ranked High School and is amazing. I love going to school there everyday. They have so many clubs and organizations that everyone has a chance to be involved. The Principal really cares about the students and has taken time out to talk to me about where I want to go to college and offering me feedback. He loves the students and their opinions. There are tons of amazing teachers and a lot of unique classes are offered. The only complaint I have is the pot holes around the school.

I am a proud Graduate of this school. I graduated in 2007 and BHS was a pretty good school then. I have not kept up with the school since I moved to another state but when I was attending I had great support from all my teachers. The teacher that impacted me the most was Mr. McAdams, he gave great advice and made learning fun. I really hope the current students are not taking BHS for granted because it truly is a good school if you take advantage of all it has to offer.

BHS is a great school in a great neighborhood. Everyone at BHS has one goal which is to help their students perform their best and become a better and knowledgeable individual that can help themselves and the community.

BHS is a hidden gem! I have had nothing but a positive experience at BHS. My child is thriving here both academically and socially, The teachers are caring, and the principle is great, and the staff is wonderful. The communication between school and home is terrific and I appreciate knowing what is going on, "The Daily Bulletin" email is so great!! There are also wonderful opportunities to join clubs and sports. It's a beautiful school and I highly recommend BHS.

We love BHS! This school has TONS of school spirit. The teachers and staff are simply fantastic. The use of technology is terrific. Our teachers care so much and do all they can for the students. I can't think of a better high school than this!

I went to BHS for my junior and senior year and loved it. The school had enough room for all the students. The princeple and teachers were great. I loved BHS and was very ready to attend an in state college where i did very well.

GHS is an excellent school to have your children. I have had one graduate from GHS and two others currently there. Their quality of education has been superior. My oldest has had a smooth transition to college much in part to the rigor that was in her coursework at GHS. It prepared her well! GHS has a rich heritage and I am excited to see how the new principal builds upon this.

GHS is a great school period. Even though I was there for only two years this school made into a better student and person. Their Performing Arts program is amazing! The students are well behaved and care about their education. Then there is the teachers, they were amazing, all of them were extremely skilled in the job and had a deep passion to teach students, not just in education, but in teaching them to be great people.
GHS is a great school! My three children graduated from there and they were well-prepared for the rigor of college.

I graduated from GHS in 2008 after transferring from a nearby district. By far, GHS is the best high school in the area. The teachers and administrators are excellent and truly want every student to succeed. There are tons of challenging and interesting courses, AP and otherwise. There are too many clubs and sports to count, so there is always a great way for students to be involved. No other school prepares students for the real world as well as GHS does. My friends who went to other high schools were simply lost compared to myself and friends at GHS. Anyone who has negative feelings about GHS simply failed to realize and take advantage of the wonderful opportunity that they were given.

GHS is an excellent school in many ways. They have high academic expectations, but are willing to help students meet them. Special education teachers and counselors are caring and dedicated. There are programs to prevent exclusion and bullying. The theater program and drama club are excellent. The honors and AP classes are world-class. I can't say enough good thing about GHS!

My family has had a great experience at GHS. My son was admitted to numerous top notch colleges, my daughters are thriving, and we love the community. GHS has an unfair bad rep - it's a beautifully diverse school in a gorgeous facility. The many satisfied families who are part of the GHS community can attest, it's a special place to be.
I have FOUR children who graduated from GHS and all of them are doing extremely well. This is a terrific HS in every way and prepares students for the challanges they will face in the future.
GHS is a wonderful school that has devoted, professional teachers that encourage each student to perform to their greatest ability.

GCHS is a terrific school! I put three kids through there and nothing but positive experiences. I have watched my peers struggle with the private school decision for high school, especially with their kids coming out of private elementary schools, but we had no such concern with GCHS. First class teachers, great administration that is smart and caring, and an excellent education. Small town values with big city resources!
GHS was great for academics, arts, music and sport teams. All of our children recently completed university with an excellent start in their careers and their own families.
This is my daughter's second year in Prep. It is an amazing school. They offer the children so much and the academics are great. They have a great support system for all children.

This school is an amazing school with lots of teacher and parent over achievers support. They excel at EVERYTHING they attempt and don't settle for anything less. It's more of a college prep school. The whole community raises these kids and many of the teachers are also parents of the students.
Great school for college prep. Wide range of academic options. Award winning extra curricular activities.

Great college prep school. I have been impressed by the caring faculty and well-balanced students - encorporating religion, education, sports, and community service into the curriculum.
